mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly growth rate in real GDP (GDPC1) relative to the prior quarter indicates expanding economic activity, which increases corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical GDP growth correlates with equity market performance
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of quarters with positive GDP growth (GDPC1 QoQ > 0%).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.5 percentage points from the prior month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Unemployment rate spikes have historically preceded market downturns
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months with UNRATE rise > 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous acceleration in inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3% month-over-month and unchanged federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) for two consecutive months signals persistent inflation without policy accommodation, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL MoM > 0.3% and FEDFUNDS unchanged for two months.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL YoY > 5%), a monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% signals manufacturing contraction, triggering recession fears and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months with INDPRO decline > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.4 million units indicates residential market contraction, reducing consumer confidence and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Housing market downturns have preceded equity market corrections
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months with HOUST < 1.4 million.

mechanism_narrative: When labor market tightness (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% month-over-month) coincides with weak consumer spending (RSAFS growth < 0.2% month-over-month), it indicates a consumption-labor mismatch, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM and RSAFS growth < 0.2% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.5%), a monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% signals economic slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months with INDPRO decline > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month growth rate in real consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong household demand, supporting corporate revenues and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Consumer spending is a key driver of GDP growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with positive RSAFS growth.
